title: Authoring lifecycle
description: The shared `authoring` block every entity schema references — design/approvals-desk.md, design/data-ownership.md. This is a `lifecycle` field (data-ownership.md §3): the repo (Claude's generators, authoring scripts, sync paths) may only ever write the baseline (`drafted`, or `needs-lore` for a location scoped but not yet written); the Foundry Approvals Desk's own guarded promote() path (#167) is the sole legal writer of `sound`/`final`/`gradedAt`/`gradedBy`/`batchId`. There is no conflict to adjudicate, because the repo side was never a legitimate second writer of those fields.

authoring.$comment: OWNER: split by entity type, declared here because this block is shared. For every entity EXCEPT a scene brief the owner is foundry-approvals-desk: status/gradedAt/gradedBy/batchId may only be raised to 'sound'/'final' by the Desk's own promote()/cutItem() paths (#167, #171). For a SCENE BRIEF the owner is scene-signoff (tools/scene-signoff/seal.mjs -> core/promote.mjs's seal()), the sole legal writer of 'live' and of the `review` block, and it may only write them from a completed Sign-Off conversation (design/scene-signoff.md). Every generator, authoring script and sync path emits 'drafted' (or 'needs-lore') and otherwise leaves this block alone -- assertNotPromotedStatus() guards all four advanced values. note/uncertainty/dependsOn are repo-authored input TO a reviewer, not its output, and stay freely editable here.

status.description: needs-lore: scoped/promoted with a note but no written content yet -- a queue pointed at Claude, not Ingram (the Desk's out-tray). drafted: written, unread -- grants nothing: not citable as canon, not syncable, not player-visible. sound: read -- the substance is right, may now be built on and cited as canon. final: read -- the words themselves are right, safe to put in front of players verbatim. cut: read and killed -- not a failure, a decision (design/approvals-desk.md §2/§6); the item stays on record rather than vanishing, same as data/audio/review.json's 'rejected'. Only the Desk's own promote()/cutItem() paths may write 'sound', 'final' or 'cut'; every other writer emits 'drafted' or 'needs-lore'. live: SCENE BRIEFS ONLY -- all four Sign-Off passes cleared and Ingram sealed it; the material is ready for actual players to enjoy and the scene can be run at the table as written. The top rung, and the only status a scene brief is ever promoted to: for a runnable unit there is no useful difference between 'the substance is right' and 'the words are right', because running it needs both (design/scene-signoff.md §3).

review.description: The Sign-Off record (design/scene-signoff.md). Scene briefs only, written pass by pass as the conversation happens, which is what makes sealing enforceable by construction: seal() refuses a scene whose record does not show all four passes CLEAR. Null until the first pass runs. Lives on the entity rather than in a log file, per the Desk's own no-new-storage-bin rule.

checklistVersion.description: The data/campaign/signoff-checklist.json version this scene was reviewed against. When that file's version rises, a sealed scene with a lower number is STALE against the specific checks added since, and re-clearing it is a targeted look at those alone -- not a fresh review. This field is the whole extensibility mechanism.

verdict.description: CLEAR: nothing left worth doing in this pass. FIX: a bounded, enumerated list of changes, capped at two rounds (design/scene-signoff.md §4). STOP: a fault editing cannot repair -- the scene needs rewriting or cutting, and the Sign-Off ends. BLOCKED: waiting on Ingram to draw, place or decide something; a legitimate resting state, Place only.

rounds.description: How many times this pass ran. Two rounds of FIX is the cap; a third run must CLEAR.

note.description: One line: what this pass actually changed, or why it cleared with findings outstanding.

passes.description: One entry per Sign-Off pass. `seam` was added 2026-09-22 with checklist v4 -- five passes, not four. This list and core/promote.mjs's SIGNOFF_PASSES must agree, and test/tier1-signoff.test.mjs asserts they do: an omission here makes a real verdict unwritable, because additionalProperties is false and the write fails validation rather than being ignored.

waived.description: Required checks deliberately declined, each with its reason. A waiver is a decision on the record, not a suppression flag -- the reason is worth more to the next reader than a silent exemption (design/scene-audit.md §8's own rule).

notApplicable.description: Checks that cannot apply to this scene, each with the reason -- NOT the same thing as `waived`. A waiver says "this applies and I am declining it"; n/a says "this cannot apply here". Only the first is a decision worth seeing on a board, and conflating them was how 7 unanswerable checks on a montage had to be either invented or silently skipped (design/scene-signoff.md §4a). Most structural cases are decided once, for the whole corpus, by a check's own appliesWhenAuto; this list is for the rest.

sessionRef.description: Which Sign-Off conversation this record came out of, so a decision can be traced back to the exchange that made it.

note.description: The rough brief this item was authored/scoped from -- e.g. a gazetteer drawing session's note. Repo-authored; corrections append, they do not overwrite.

uncertainty.description: What Claude was unsure about when writing this -- "I invented a surname here", "this assumes a rule nobody has confirmed". design/approvals-desk.md §4: the single highest-value thing on the Desk's card, since it points straight at the part most likely to be wrong. Repo-authored; clearing it is the Desk's business, not a rule enforced here.

dependsOn.description: Other entities (by id, any type) this item's own soundness assumes. Lets the Desk flag a dependency that is itself still drafted (design/approvals-desk.md §4) -- a safety check, not a second ordering axis.

gradedAt.description: When the Desk last changed `status`. Null until first graded. Desk-owned.

gradedBy.description: Who graded it. Named rather than assumed, per data-ownership.md's rule that a lifecycle field's advanced values have exactly one legal writer. Desk-owned.

batchId.description: Set when this item was cleared as part of a machine-proposed batch rather than read individually (design/approvals-desk.md §5), so a problem traced back later can see it was a sweep, not a read. Desk-owned; null for an individually-graded item.
